open-v2.catalog-linkage-review.title: Open-v2 catalog linkage review
open-v2.catalog-linkage-review.version_scope: Retained open-v2 table, key, projection, relationship, and caveat conclusions derived during the schema-version-3 Phase 2 review.
notes: This versioned record preserves reviewed implementation conclusions, including unresolved relationship behavior, without making the active catalog self-citing.
It is not a substitute for maintainer confirmation of clinical workflow semantics.

open-v2.maintainer-clarification-2026-07.title: Open-v2 maintainer clarification on representation and provenance
open-v2.maintainer-clarification-2026-07.version_scope: Open-v2 linked-exam, multimodal descriptor, aggregation, pathology, report, risk, demographic, laterality, and date semantics reviewed on 2026-07-29 and retained in the repository clarification record.
notes: Confirms same-episode linked accessions, descriptor-versus-modality boundaries, mammography-only Boolean aggregates, minimum pathology-severity rollups, synthetic contralateral findings, age handling, legal-sex and release-version meanings, context-dependent null laterality, procedure-associated pathology-code behavior, report-version sequencing, clinical-time risk calculation, and consistent within-patient date shifts.
Ordinary risk outputs are tentatively believed to use percentage points, but the risk table has not been validated in depth.

Retains unknown system-specific code mappings, report addendum linkage, risk-field variants, most sentinel meanings, measurement units, MRI ambiguities, and model versions for later internal investigation.
There is no universal delimiter, ordering, or null convention across loosely structured coded fields; absent field-specific evidence, preserve source strings and treat null as unknown or missing.

open-v2.release-legend.title: EMBED V2 open-data clinical legend
open-v2.release-legend.version_scope: Legend distributed for the open-v2 clinical-table release.
notes: The legend supports released header and code meanings but is not assumed exhaustive.
Legend content does not establish temporal availability, row identity, or null semantics.

open-v2.release-schema.title: EMBED V2 open-data Parquet footer schemas
open-v2.release-schema.locator: open-v2 clinical table Parquet footer schemas
open-v2.release-schema.version_scope: Physical columns, types, and schema nullability for the open-v2 clinical-table release.
notes: Footer schemas establish representation but not clinical values or empirical distributions.
The registered footer verification does not inspect clinical rows.

open-v2.assessment-recommendation-contex.title: Open-v2 assessment and recommendation context
open-v2.assessment-recommendation-contex.summary: Assessment and recommendation are distinct finding-level fields whose clinical and temporal roles must not be collapsed.

claims.statement: Open-v2 represents imaging assessment and imaging recommendation as separate columns at imaging-finding grain.
caveats: Physical co-location does not make the fields semantically interchangeable.

claims.statement: The released assessment codes identify distinct BI-RADS states and must not be reduced to one simple ordinal scale.
caveats: Code membership alone does not establish workflow validity for a particular exam type.

claims.statement: Recommendation strings come from a loose multi-site MagView reporting schema with expected formatting heterogeneity.
caveats: Preserve the source string rather than imposing a canonical grammar.

claims.statement: Mappings for valid recommendation codes absent from the released legend are currently unknown; there is no single authoritative owner or versioned dictionary across the contributing clinical systems.
caveats: Resolving a code requires system-specific investigation and data processing; do not guess or silently normalize undocumented recommendation codes.

claims.statement: The assessment and recommendation columns in combined_anon are convenience projections, not proof of value equality or contemporaneous availability.
caveats: Use the canonical imaging-finding binding when feature provenance matters.
Do not derive an outcome label from assessment or recommendation without a declared task and temporal anchor.
Public pathway guidance does not establish that open-v2 rows form a complete screening-to-diagnostic sequence.

open-v2.demographic-administrative-conte.title: Open-v2 demographic and administrative semantics
open-v2.demographic-administrative-conte.summary: Open-v2 age, ancestry, legal-sex, and release-version fields retain source-specific definitions and deidentification caveats.

claims.statement: The age-at-exam, menarche-age, menopause-age, and pregnancy-age fields are measured in years; values such as zero are data-quality errors rather than documented sentinel codes.
caveats: The specific pregnancy event represented by pregnancy age remains unresolved.

claims.statement: Age at exam is calculated from the patient birth date and study date after both dates receive the same within-patient shift; it is otherwise unchanged except that ages greater than or equal to 90 are top-coded to 89.
caveats: The shifted calendar dates must not be interpreted literally.

claims.statement: The Ashkenazi indicator represents self-identified Ashkenazi Jewish heritage recorded as a known breast-cancer risk factor.
caveats: Completeness, reliability, encoding, and null semantics are not established.

claims.statement: The released gender-description field represents patient legal sex at the time of the exam.
caveats: This field does not represent gender identity.

claims.statement: The EMBED data-version field records the first EMBED release version in which the element was included.
caveats: It is not a per-row processing-lineage or schema-version guarantee.
Do not convert data-quality errors into sentinel meanings without field-specific evidence.
Administrative legal sex, gender identity, and self-identified heritage are distinct constructs.

open-v2.linked-exam-context.title: Open-v2 linked-exam references
open-v2.linked-exam-context.summary: Linked accession fields identify same-episode exams linked at study time, with expected data-quality and release-coverage edge cases.

claims.statement: A linked accession is an optional reference and is not guaranteed to resolve to an open-v2 exam row.
caveats: Treat accession identifiers as opaque and release-scoped.

claims.statement: Multiple imaging-finding or wide rows may reference the same linked exam, so joined exam attributes can repeat at the source grain.
caveats: This is a row-multiplication hazard, not an empirical frequency claim.

claims.statement: The linked-study flag and linked-accession presence are expected to describe the same same-episode linkage, but data-quality edge cases can violate row-wise equivalence.
caveats: Do not use one field as a missing-value repair for the other.

claims.statement: A linked accession identifies a same-episode exam linked at study time; it does not designate a prior or follow-up exam.
caveats: Use the linked exams' study dates for their temporal context.
Linked references describe relationship metadata and are not executable joins.
Release filtering and ordinary data-quality artifacts can leave expected link or flag invariants unsatisfied in edge cases.

open-v2.multimodal-finding-context.title: Open-v2 multimodal finding context
open-v2.multimodal-finding-context.summary: The imaging-finding surface contains mammography, ultrasound, and MRI descriptor families without proving modality presence from descriptor nulls.

claims.statement: Open-v2 imaging_findings_anon exposes distinct mammography, ultrasound, and MRI descriptor columns.
caveats: A shared table surface does not make modality-specific descriptors interchangeable.

claims.statement: Exam modality is represented separately at exam grain and should remain distinct from individual descriptor fields.
caveats: Cross-field modality consistency has not been registered as a validated invariant.

claims.statement: Modality-specific descriptor fields indicate presence or absence of particular finding descriptors and do not establish whether that modality was performed or available.
caveats: Use the separate exam/modality features for modality availability.

claims.statement: Exam-level and breast-side-level mass, calcification, asymmetry, and architectural-distortion fields are Boolean summaries aggregated only from mammography findings, including FFDM, synthetic 2D, and DBT.
caveats: These summaries do not aggregate ultrasound or MRI descriptors.

claims.statement: After excluding finding number -9, accession and finding number identify a distinct clinical finding within an accession; -9 identifies a derived synthetic contralateral negative finding implied by a non-negative finding on the other breast but not explicitly entered in MagView.
caveats: Synthetic contralateral negatives are derived records.
The clinical identity can occupy multiple physical rows and is not a persistent lesion identifier across accessions, episodes, or modalities.

claims.statement: A null side attached to a clinical finding represents a bilateral finding; outside that context, null generally means unknown laterality and a null biopsy or procedure side is not bilateral.
caveats: Interpret null laterality according to the field's clinical role rather than applying a catalog-wide null rule.

claims.statement: Loosely structured coded fields do not share one guaranteed delimiter, ordering, repetition, composition, or null convention.
caveats: Without field-specific evidence, preserve source strings, treat ordering as non-informative, and treat null as unknown or missing.
Descriptor presence and modality availability are separate questions represented by different features.

open-v2.pathology-procedure-context.title: Open-v2 pathology and procedure context
open-v2.pathology-procedure-context.summary: Pathology findings carry procedure, report, surgery, diagnosis-slot, and severity fields with non-unique links back to imaging.

claims.statement: Open-v2 stores pathology findings in a separate pathology-finding-grain table with procedure, report, surgery, and diagnosis fields.
caveats: The table grain does not establish a unique clinical row identity.

claims.statement: The registered pathology-to-imaging association uses accession, finding side, and finding number, but is optional and can match multiple rows in either direction.
caveats: Joining can multiply rows and incomplete tuples require an explicit policy.

claims.statement: The side component of the registered imaging relationship is finding side, not biopsy side.
caveats: Do not substitute bside when following the declared table relationship.

claims.statement: Path1 through path10 are procedure-associated pathology descriptor codes, generally ordered by severity group; slot position, within-group order, and duplicate occurrences are not informative for decision-making.
caveats: Duplicate codes are not intended but may occur and are equivalent to one occurrence.

claims.statement: Pathology descriptor codes observed in open-v2 but absent from the released legend are valid source-system codes with mappings that are currently unknown; there is no single authoritative owner or versioned dictionary across the contributing clinical systems.
caveats: Retain unknown codes as observed; resolving one requires system-specific investigation and data processing.

claims.statement: Pathology severity is the inverse coded group of the most severe attached pathology descriptor: 0 invasive cancer, 1 in-situ cancer, 2 high-risk lesion, 3 borderline lesion, 4 benign finding, and 5 non-breast cancer.
caveats: Lower values are more severe; null means no attached pathology and is not benign or negative.

claims.statement: Exam-level and breast-side-level pathology severity are aggregated by taking the minimum, and therefore most severe, value among procedure-associated pathology records in the applicable group.
caveats: The inverse ordering means an ordinary numeric maximum would select the least severe value.

claims.statement: The registered open-v2 bindings expose pathology-severity values and side- and exam-level rollups but no patient-level pathology-severity result field or supplied longitudinal outcome rollup.
caveats: Absence of a supplied field does not prohibit an analyst-defined policy; it means the catalog does not designate one.

claims.statement: The registered open-v2 metadata and public pathology-attribution documentation do not establish complete capture of breast-cancer outcomes, outside-system diagnoses, or longitudinal follow-up.
caveats: This is a limitation of available evidence, not a measured estimate of missing outcomes or follow-up.
Procedure and pathology information may postdate imaging and must not be treated as contemporaneous by default.
In the classic MagView representation, distinct procedures carry distinct procedure/pathology values even when the associated finding content is otherwise duplicated.

open-v2.report-context.title: Open-v2 report lifecycle context
open-v2.report-context.summary: Reports are accession-linked records whose sequence orders successive MagView report versions; source heterogeneity can produce duplicate natural tuples and the addendum-flag relationship remains unverified.

claims.statement: Open-v2 stores anonymized accession-linked radiology report text with the associated imaging-exam study date and MagView report-version sequence.
caveats: Report content was not read while authoring the catalog.

claims.statement: No tested natural tuple uniquely identifies every report row in the registered open-v2 review.
caveats: The technical export index is not a documented durable report identifier.

claims.statement: MagView increments rseq when a new report version is created; within an accession the minimum represented sequence is earliest and the maximum is latest.
caveats: The specific origin of rseq zero is unknown, but zero participates in the same minimum-to-maximum chronology.
Ordinary source-system and site heterogeneity can produce duplicate natural tuples.

claims.statement: Reports with rseq greater than the accession minimum are expected to be later report versions and generally addendums, but real-world exceptions and the relationship to the processing-derived imaging addendum_flag have not been directly validated.
caveats: A later report version may not constitute an addendum in the strict clinical sense; do not infer that one flag identifies a particular report revision.

claims.statement: Joining report rows to finding-grain tables by accession can multiply both report and finding rows.
caveats: Aggregate or select reports only under an explicit report policy.
Use minimum and maximum rseq for earliest and latest represented report versions; do not rely on tuple uniqueness.
Treat report text as potentially sensitive and do not expose raw values through this context service.

open-v2.risk-context.title: Open-v2 risk-assessment context
open-v2.risk-context.summary: Risk outputs were calculated during clinical care in MagView and ordinary values are tentatively believed to use percentage points, but the risk table, field variants, exceptional values, and model versions require internal investigation.

claims.statement: Open-v2 stores named IBIS and NCI numeric outputs at risk-assessment grain with patient, accession, and study-date references.
caveats: A released name is not a complete clinical definition.

claims.statement: Ordinary NCI and IBIS outputs are tentatively believed to use percentage points, but the risk table has not been validated in depth. IBISPOP10, IBISPOPL, and IBIS_TD1 through IBIS_TD4 lack confirmed definitions; meanings of -35, -2, and 100 and the generating model versions are also unknown.
caveats: Treat percentage-point formatting as tentative and do not infer a comparable range from numeric physical type.

claims.statement: The risk-to-exam relationship is optional and does not establish that every exam has a risk record.
caveats: No empirical coverage measurement belongs in this catalog.

claims.statement: The released risk scores were calculated during clinical care and extracted from the breast-imaging MagView EHR system.
caveats: Clinical-time calculation does not by itself establish the exact calculation timestamp within the study episode.
Risk output and BI-RADS assessment are different constructs and must not be substituted for one another.
No field is approved for modeling or release merely because it appears in risk_anon.

open-v2.temporal-availability-context.title: Open-v2 temporal availability guardrail
open-v2.temporal-availability-context.summary: Open-v2 dates use a consistent per-patient random shift, preserving within-patient ordering and date differences while obscuring absolute calendar dates.

claims.statement: Open-v2 exposes exam, procedure, and pathology-report date fields in separate clinical surfaces.
caveats: Absolute calendar values are anonymized and must not be interpreted literally.

claims.statement: EMBED applies one consistent random date shift per patient across that patient's dates, so within-patient ordering and date differences are reliable while absolute day, month, and year are not.
caveats: Do not compare absolute calendar dates across patients.

claims.statement: Co-location of fields in combined_anon does not establish that they were observed at the same clinical time.
caveats: The wide table's construction remains unresolved.

claims.statement: Combined_anon projects patient, exam, finding, procedure, and pathology fields onto wide rows; those projections do not establish that repeated attributes are authoritative, that each clinical object has wide-row identity, or that fields were co-available.
caveats: Use canonical or co-located normalized bindings to understand object representation before relying on a wide projection.

claims.statement: The registered open-v2 feature bindings contain exam, procedure, and pathology-report dates but no specimen-collection date or universal downstream-availability timestamp.
caveats: A missing binding does not prove that the clinical event or availability transition did not occur.
Task-specific cohort, follow-up, label, and modality-inclusion choices are analysis policies rather than dataset claims; agents must choose and defend them outside the portable catalog.

coverage.open-v2.specimen-time.subject: time.specimen-collection
coverage.open-v2.specimen-time.summary: Specimen collection is clinically meaningful, but the registered open-v2 bindings contain no supported specimen-collection date feature.
caveats: Do not substitute procedure date or pathology-report date.

coverage.open-v2.downstream-availability.subject: time.downstream-availability
coverage.open-v2.downstream-availability.summary: The registered open-v2 bindings contain event and documentation dates but no supported universal timestamp for when each downstream field became available.
caveats: Do not infer field availability from wide-row co-location.
Do not coalesce or substitute event, documentation, or imaging-exam dates as fallback values for one another.
A different temporal semantic may be evaluated as a separately named endpoint or sensitivity analysis, not used to fill missingness in the selected endpoint.

coverage.open-v2.outcome-capture.subject: open-v2.pathology-procedure-context
coverage.open-v2.outcome-capture.summary: The available metadata does not establish complete capture of breast-cancer outcomes, outside-system diagnoses, or longitudinal follow-up.
caveats: No empirical capture rate belongs in the portable catalog.
Absence of a represented diagnosis is not proof of disease absence.

coverage.open-v2.risk-probability-calibr.subject: open-v2.risk-context
coverage.open-v2.risk-probability-calibr.summary: Open-v2 risk fields are physically represented, but their scale, units, exceptional values, model versions, horizon semantics, and readiness for probability-calibration metrics have not been validated.
caveats: This unresolved readiness statement does not mark the physical risk fields unsupported.
Association or ranking analyses may be possible when score interpretation and remaining uncertainty are explicitly qualified.

coverage.open-v2.patient-pathology-aggre.subject: aggregation.pathology-severity-to-patient
coverage.open-v2.patient-pathology-aggre.summary: Open-v2 supplies no canonical patient-level pathology severity field or universal longitudinal outcome rollup.
caveats: Any patient-level policy remains analysis specific.

coverage.open-v2.pathology-severity-to-s.subject: aggregation.pathology-severity-to-side
coverage.open-v2.pathology-severity-to-s.summary: Open-v2 supplies a breast-side pathology-severity result concept whose verified rollup takes the minimum represented severity in the applicable side group.
caveats: Support for the rollup does not remove laterality-attribution or unattached-pathology limitations.

coverage.open-v2.pathology-severity-to-e.subject: aggregation.pathology-severity-to-exam
coverage.open-v2.pathology-severity-to-e.summary: Open-v2 supplies an exam pathology-severity result concept whose verified rollup takes the minimum represented severity in the applicable exam group.
caveats: Support for the rollup does not establish pathology availability at exam time or complete outcome capture.

coverage.open-v2.finding-pathology-attri.subject: clinical.finding-pathology-observation
coverage.open-v2.finding-pathology-attri.summary: A physical finding-to-pathology tuple is registered, but its attribution is optional, incomplete, and many-to-many.
caveats: Supported linkage metadata is not complete outcome ascertainment.

coverage.open-v2.pathology-code-meanings.subject: pathology.diagnosis_code_slot
coverage.open-v2.pathology-code-meanings.summary: Some valid source-system pathology codes have no mapping in the released legend or a single authoritative cross-system dictionary.
caveats: Retain unknown codes without guessing or silently normalizing them.

coverage.open-v2.imaging-episode.subject: breast_imaging_episode
coverage.open-v2.imaging-episode.summary: Same-episode linked accessions are represented, but no canonical episode identifier or complete episode-construction surface is established.
caveats: Do not infer prior or follow-up order from the linked-accession relation.

join_hazards: Use accession for the exam edge; retain side only for side-grain identity.

relationship_binding_paths.description: Traverse from each candidate pathology row's accession to its associated candidate exam, then from that exam to the patient before comparing the candidate with qualifying index exams for the same patient.
caveats: The path is descriptive binding metadata, not an executable join or a guarantee of complete longitudinal outcome capture.
Do not require the candidate pathology accession to equal the index exam accession.
